counterexamples.observed: The original lowerer emitted cc_int_div for every program; under -Wall -Wextra -Werror, 8/9 representative non-division programs failed as unused-function.
counterexamples.fix: Emit checked integer helpers only when reachable emitted code requires them.

counterexamples.observed: Programs with an entry plus an unrelated sibling function failed -Werror=unused-function; a zero-argument entry also failed on unused argv.
counterexamples.fix: Emit only the transitive call closure reachable from entry, preserve all functions in typed IR, and explicitly mark argv/declared parameters as intentionally usable/unusable at the C boundary.

counterexamples.observed: Python reference evaluation used unbounded integers while C uses int64_t: INT64_MAX+1, INT64_MIN-1 and large multiplication produced different results.
counterexamples.fix: Checked Int64 add/sub/mul/div in both evaluator and emitted C with deterministic overflow/error boundaries.

counterexamples.observed: Direct recursion reached the evaluator recursion guard but GCC -Werror rejected infinite recursion; mutual recursion was also not a defined executable pure-slice contract.
counterexamples.fix: Reject recursive call cycles in the current pure-function slice with RECURSIVE_CALL_CYCLE before typed IR release.

counterexamples.observed: strtoll/strtod/atoi paths silently accepted or clamped invalid typed input: oversized Int, abc, trailing junk, NaN/Inf and arbitrary Bool integers.
counterexamples.fix: Fail-closed typed CLI decoders: Int RC70, Real RC71, Bool RC72.

counterexamples.observed: Out-of-range Int/Real literals entered IR; INT64_MIN textual lowering triggered GCC -Werror and 1e309 lowered to undeclared C token inf.
counterexamples.fix: Reject out-of-range/underflow literals and lower exact INT64_MIN using the C macro.

counterexamples.observed: Reference evaluator compares String contents, while C ==/!= compared pointers; two distinct char arrays containing the same bytes yielded evaluator eq=true/ne=false but native eq=false/ne=true.
counterexamples.fix: Lower String equality/inequality through strcmp content comparison.

counterexamples.observed: Python float division by zero raised while native double division did not share the same deterministic error behavior.
counterexamples.fix: Use checked real division helper; +/-0 denominator produces REAL_DIVISION_BY_ZERO / native RC73.
